archetypes.name: architecture
archetypes.rationale: The change coordinates rc=14 removal across a large surface of scripts and markdown docs; stale references outside the diff could silently misbehave.
archetypes.prompt_body: Audit whether any files not touched by this diff still reference exit code 14, the old `DRIFT_TRIGGER_FIRED` gate, the `_postplan_emit_drift_section` function, or the old `_postplan_rc=14` / `POSTPLAN_RC=14` case arms. Check shell scripts (`review-design-step3-loop.sh` callsites, any harnesses not in the diff), markdown reference files, and the Makefile. Verify that the asymmetry between `assert_postplan_thin_fence` (still checks `DRIFT_` / `BASELINE_` grep pins) and `assert_postplan_reference_thin_fence` (those pins removed) is intentional and matches the updated contracts in `SKILL.md` vs `approval-gates.md`. Verify that the `case` arm lists in `SKILL.md`, `approval-gates.md`, `discussion-rounds.md`, and `flags.md` are all mutually consistent after the removal of arm `14`. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: code-quality
archetypes.rationale: The new drift branch in design-postplan-emit.sh calls _postplan_flush before a trailing emit and uses a temp file with append-tool-failure.sh; the parameter semantics and ordering need scrutiny.
archetypes.prompt_body: In `skills/design/scripts/design-postplan-emit.sh`, examine the new drift branch added in `_postplan_finish_merged_plan_size()`: the sequence calls `_postplan_flush || exit 1`, then `emit "⏩ 2b.5: plan-size — drift advisory..."`, then `exit 0`. Determine whether an `emit` call after `_postplan_flush` will appear on the correct output stream, or whether the flush finalizes the channel and makes the subsequent advisory invisible. Verify that the `append-tool-failure.sh` invocation uses `--output-file` as a source-file parameter (a file to read the warning body from) rather than a destination — check how other callers in the same script use this flag. Confirm that `$PLUGIN_ROOT` is reliably set in the script's execution context (not just `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT`). Check that the `rm -f "$_drift_log"` cleanup is robust if `append-tool-failure.sh` fails (i.e., the `|| true` on the preceding call does not suppress a missing file). Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
